Trump Addresses Potential MOAB Strike on Iran

In an interview with Newsmax aired Thursday evening, Trump dismissed the need for nuclear weapons in the conflict, saying, "I wouldn’t use nuclear. We don’t have to. We’re the greatest nuclear power in the world."

Asked about reports that Washington was considering deploying the GBU-43/B Massive Ordnance Air Blast (MOAB), commonly known as the "Mother of All Bombs," Trump noted that the weapon is conventional rather than nuclear.

"It’s like a tiny nuclear bomb," he said, describing its destructive power while noting that it is not a nuclear weapon. He did not directly confirm or deny whether the U.S. was considering using it against Iran.
When asked whether he would deploy U.S. troops on the ground in Iran, Trump responded, "No, I don’t see that, I don’t see it."

The MOAB is the largest non-nuclear bomb in the U.S. arsenal. American forces used it in combat for the first time in 2017 against Islamic State of Iraq and Syria (ISIS) militants in Afghanistan, CNBC reported.
The White House did not immediately respond to Benzinga’s request for comment.

Strait of Hormuz Faces Rising Shipping Threats
Meanwhile, commercial shipping faces growing risks in the Strait of Hormuz following a series of attacks in the strategic waterway.

The U.K. Maritime Trade Operations said the threat remained "severe" after the Singapore-registered container ship GFS Pride was hit by an unidentified projectile, caught fire and sank. The agency said "deliberate hostile action" was highly likely and reported eight attacks in the strait since Oct. 11, raising concerns over the safety of a critical global energy shipping route.
